subject: Intermittent packet truncation to Hearthside on-prem after firewall maintenance
messages:
From: Jenna Park <ops@hearthside.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Derek Lowe <neteng@columina.tech>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packet truncation to Redwood private endpoint after FW change

Hi Irene,

We saw a spike in failed API responses to our private deployment (Hearthside VPC) starting after an evening firewall policy push last night. Symptoms: 5xx from the service, intermittent TCP RSTs and application-layer truncation (payloads cut ~1460 bytes). We ran a quick tcpdump and attached the capture.

Observed:
- Most clients are fine, but a subset in our on-prem environment show repeated retransmits and truncated payloads.
- Traceroutes show a hop where MTU drops from 1500 to 1300.
- We suspect either MTU/MSS miscoordination or an aggressive security device doing packet rewrite/truncate.

Can Redwood confirm if anything changed on the private edge (SNAT, MTU, SG rules) around 03/26 22:00 PDT? This is impacting production jobs.

Attachments: pcap-hearthside-trace-20280327.pcap

Thanks,
Jenna Park
Senior Ops Engineer
Hearthside Labs
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <ops@hearthside.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet truncation to Redwood private endpoint after FW change

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Jenna — and for the pcap. We haven’t made any intentional config changes to the dedicated private edge for Hearthside since the weekend rollout, but I’m escalating to network ops and our private-deploy team.

Initial triage notes (quick):
- Shown in the pcap: repeated MSS/DF interactions and cases where downstream hop returns ICMP "Fragmentation needed but DF set" with MTU ~1300.
- Our SNAT pool is fine; no mass connection resets from our side.
- We will check the private edge MTU and any inline security appliances that could modify TCP windows or strip ICMP.

Immediate ask: can you share one example client IP (from the pcap) and the exact timestamp you saw the failed application request? That helps correlate connection IDs on our side.

I’m putting Marissa and Vanessa on this thread for routing / SG checks and to confirm whether a temporary MSS clamp or bypass route is advisable. We’ll update within the hour.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Staff Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <ops@hearthside.com>, Derek Lowe <neteng@columina.tech>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Packet truncation to Redwood private endpoint — immediate network checks

Marissa / Vanessa — short summary and data included below. Customer shows DF/Fragmentation ICMP with effective MTU ~1300 on the path. pcap attached by customer (see pcap-hearthside-trace-20280327.pcap).

What I need from you:
- Marissa: verify MTU settings on the private edge (both physical NIC and VXLAN/GRE endpoints) for the Hearthside tenant; report any recent firmware or config pushes.
- Vanessa: check security group and private edge IPS/NGFW logs around 2028-03-26T22:00-23:30Z for any packet rewrite or TCP stream termination patterns; specifically look for ICMP rate-limit actions and TCP MSS adjusting.

Potential mitigation options (if MTU mismatch confirmed):
- Apply MSS clamping at the edge for customer traffic (temporary).
- Add a small bypass (non-IPS path) for Hearthside while we validate their appliance.
- Work with customer to enable path MTU discovery ICMP messages (if their firewall blocks them).

I grabbed the example client IP from the pcap: 10.34.12.87 (source) -> our private egress IP 172.31.4.22 at 2028-03-27T07:58:12Z. Customer, please verify this lines up with your capture.

Irene

> Excerpt from customer's pcap (from Jenna):
> 07:58:12.123 IP 10.34.12.87.51432 > 172.31.4.22.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 64240, length 1460
> 07:58:12.124 ICMP 172.31.4.22 > 10.34.12.87: Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu = 1300)
> 07:58:12.130 TCP 10.34.12.87.51432 > 172.31.4.22.443: Flags [R]  (reset)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <ops@hearthside.com>, Derek Lowe <neteng@columina.tech>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Packet truncation to Redwood private endpoint — immediate network checks

Quick findings:
- Edge host hf-edge-17 (Hearthside tenant) shows interface mtu configured to 1500 on the physical NIC, but the VXLAN overlay endpoint had a manual MTU set to 1400 (recent change 03/26 by a firmware update pushed by vendor).
- No automated SNAT changes; conntrack counts steady.
- IPS logs show the inline NGFW (vendor: FenGuard) responding to oversized frames by dropping them when DF=1 and returning ICMP "fragmentation needed" with an enforced MTU of 1300 (this is an NGFW behaviour introduced in 03/26 policy rev A).

Action taken:
- I applied a temporary MSS clamp on the edge for the Hearthside route (/sbin/iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu) — rolling to prod for tenant traffic only.
- Opened a vendor ticket with FenGuard to request clarification on why the device rewrites MTU to 1300 and whether we can switch to returning ICMP unreachable rather than dropping.

Customer impact: early signs show a marked drop in truncated payloads after MSS clamp applied. But we need Hearthside to confirm client-side success and whether any flows remain impacted.

Next steps:
- Vanessa: follow-up on SG rules — I’ll keep the MSS clamp in place until we have vendor resolution or we implement a bypass path.
- Jenna / Derek: please confirm if your team still sees truncation after 10:30 PDT. If yes, attach a short pcap of an affected connection post-10:30.

— Marissa
Network Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Park <ops@hearthside.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Derek Lowe <neteng@columina.tech>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet truncation to Redwood private endpoint after FW change — resolved for now

Irene / Marissa / Vanessa,

Confirming: after your MSS clamp went live, the error rate dropped to baseline and no new truncated payloads observed in our production window. We did a controlled test (same client IP 10.34.12.87) and the capture shows the full payloads now. Attached is a short post-mitigation pcap.

We’ll keep the customer-side appliance in analysis with FenGuard; Derek will coordinate with their vendor. Please keep us posted on vendor findings and any permanent config you'd like us to apply.

Thanks for the quick turn-around. Recommended follow-up:
- Permanent fix: align overlay MTU with physical and update vendor policy so NGFW does not enforce aggressive MTU rewrite.
- Postmortem: brief runbook entry on MSS clamp as temporary mitigation and detection alerts for DF/Fragmentation ICMP.

Best,
Jenna
Senior Ops Engineer
Hearthside Labs
